title: Best Toshiba Dehumidifier (2026): TDDP5013ES2 & Lineup Ranked
dek: A famous electronics badge on Midea-built hardware. Here's which Toshiba size to buy, what the model numbers mean and where the brand falls short.
description: The best Toshiba dehumidifier for each space, from the 20-pint TDDP2013ES2 to the 50-pint TDDP5013ES2, plus model decoding, manual and repair tips.
intro: Toshiba is a name most people know from TVs and laptops, and that recognition gives a **Toshiba dehumidifier** an air of premium quality that lesser-known brands don't enjoy. The reality is more nuanced: ENERGY STAR's certification records list **GD Midea** as the manufacturer behind Toshiba's current dehumidifiers — the same company that builds units for several budget brands.

That isn't a knock. Midea makes some of the most efficient portable dehumidifiers sold in the U.S., and two of Toshiba's three sizes carry ENERGY STAR's Most Efficient designation. But it does mean you're paying for a badge more than for unique hardware, so it pays to compare. Below, we rank Toshiba's 20-, 35- and 50-pint models, decode the TDDP model numbers you'll see on older listings, and cover the manual, filter and repair questions owners ask most.
topPicksLead: For most bedrooms and offices, the **Toshiba 20-Pint (TDDP2013ES2)** is the best place to start; basements should step up to the 50-pint TDDP5013ES2.

products.name: Toshiba 20-Pint Dehumidifier (TDDP2013ES2)
pros: Rolls between rooms on four casters
cons: Coverage figures vary between retailer listings
products.whyWeLoveIt: A 20-pint machine is the right size for a bedroom, home office or small damp room, and Toshiba's version covers the essentials without fuss. It's also the least expensive way into the brand.
products.performance: Toshiba rates it at 20 pints a day under the current DOE test and lists coverage of up to 1,500 square feet. Casters make it easy to move with the seasons, and a hose connection lets it run continuously to a floor drain. Check the full model suffix before you buy, since closely numbered SKUs sometimes show different coverage claims. For other options in this size, see our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.name: Toshiba 35-Pint Dehumidifier (TDDP3513ES2)
pros: Sized for a large room or small basement
cons: Same Midea platform as cheaper brands
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the sweet spot of the lineup. It carries ENERGY STAR's top efficiency tier — confirmed for this exact model number — so long summer runtimes cost less, and it has enough capacity for a family room or a modest basement.
products.performance: It's rated at 35 pints a day with coverage of up to 3,000 square feet. A gravity hose lets it run unattended where there's a drain nearby. If you're deciding between this and a 50-pint, our [best dehumidifier for 1,000 sq ft](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-1000-sq-ft/) guide helps you size the space.

products.name: Toshiba 50-Pint Dehumidifier (TDDP5013ES2)
pros: Rated for up to 4,500 sq ft
cons: Independent bench test found only average drying speed
Built-in humidity reading ran a few points high in that test
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a full basement, the TDDP5013ES2 brings 50 pints of capacity, Most Efficient certification and a generous tank. It's the Toshiba most shoppers search for, and it's a solid machine — just not a standout one.
products.performance: It's rated at 50 pints a day with coverage up to 4,500 square feet. Consumer Reports lists a 15-pint internal tank and gravity drainage on this SKU. An independent bench test of the closely related TDDP5012ES2 took a little over 12 minutes to bring a test room from 90% to 40% humidity, versus 10 to 11 minutes for rivals, and found its built-in humidity reading about 4% high. If your basement lacks a floor drain, choose the pump-equipped TDDP5014RES2 instead, or compare options in our [dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.
products.notes: Because the display may read a few points high, confirm conditions with a separate hygrometer before you adjust the setpoint.

blocks.text: Consumer Reports' survey covered roughly 13,600 dehumidifiers bought by its members between 2014 and 2025, and Toshiba landed in the small group of brands earning the highest predicted-reliability rating, alongside Midea, Keystone and Perfect Aire.

We don't run a lab. We compare each model's DOE 2019 capacity rating, ENERGY STAR certification and manufacturer listing, manufacturer specs for coverage and drainage, Consumer Reports' published reliability data and any independent bench measurements we can find. We also search CPSC recall records by brand and by manufacturer, and we read owner reviews for patterns such as early compressor failures.
For a brand like Toshiba, where the hardware is shared with other names, we also weigh whether a near-identical Midea-built unit offers the same performance for less.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Toshiba dehumidifier

items.label: Size by square footage
items.text: Twenty pints for a bedroom or office, 35 for a large room, 50 for a full or very damp basement. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) goes deeper.

items.label: Check the exact model number
items.text: Most Efficient certification applies to specific SKUs. Confirm the full model number, suffix included, on the ENERGY STAR listing.

items.label: Pump or gravity
items.text: The standard 50-pint drains by gravity. If the nearest drain is above the unit, buy the TDDP5014RES2 with a built-in pump.

items.label: Weigh reliability against performance
items.text: A high predicted-reliability score measures long-run failure rates, not drying speed. Both matter.

items.label: Compare its Midea-built siblings
items.text: Shared manufacturing means a similar Midea, Keystone or GE unit may cost less. Our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup compares them.

blocks.text: The "70-pint" label on the TDDP7011ES2 reflects the DOE test used before 2019, which ran at warmer conditions and produced bigger numbers. Under the current test, that class of machine rates at about 50 pints, so it's a peer of the TDDP5013ES2, not a bigger unit.

sections.heading: Toshiba dehumidifier manual, filter and repair

blocks.text: The full model number is on the rating label on the back or side of the unit. Search that number on Toshiba's home-appliance support site or the retailer's product page to download the owner's manual. Midea holds the Toshiba home-appliance license in the U.S., so support contacts in newer manuals may route through the license holder.

Toshiba units use a washable mesh filter behind the intake grille. Slide it out every couple of weeks during heavy use, rinse it with lukewarm water, let it dry completely and reinstall it. You shouldn't need to buy a replacement unless the mesh is damaged.

items: **Not collecting water:** check that the room is above about 41°F and that the coils aren't frosted. Our [not collecting water guide](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) walks through the rest.
**Shuts off right away:** reseat the bucket; the full-tank float switch may think it's full.
**Icing on the coils:** clean the filter, move the unit away from walls and let it defrost before restarting.
**Error code on the display:** look it up in your model's manual, unplug for a few minutes to reset, and contact support if it returns.
**Compressor won't start after the first year:** owners report occasional failures just past warranty, so register the unit and keep your receipt.

blocks.text: The **Toshiba 20-Pint (TDDP2013ES2)** is the best entry point for bedrooms and offices, the **35-Pint (TDDP3513ES2)** is the efficient mid-size pick, and the **50-Pint (TDDP5013ES2)** is the one for a full basement — with the pump-equipped TDDP5014RES2 for spaces without a floor drain. Toshiba's reliability scores are strong and its recall record is clean, but independent data shows its drying speed is average, and the same Midea hardware sells under other names. Compare prices with its siblings in our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide before you buy.

faqs.q: What is the best Toshiba dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a bedroom or office, the 20-pint TDDP2013ES2. For a large room, the 35-pint TDDP3513ES2, which is ENERGY STAR Most Efficient certified. For a full basement, the 50-pint TDDP5013ES2, or the TDDP5014RES2 if you need a built-in pump.

faqs.q: Is the Toshiba TDDP5013ES2 worth it?
faqs.a: It's a solid basement dehumidifier with Most Efficient certification, a 15-pint tank and a strong brand reliability score. An independent bench test of its predecessor found only average drying speed, though, so compare it with similarly priced Midea-built units before buying.

ENERGY STAR's certification records list GD Midea as the manufacturer of Toshiba's current dehumidifiers. Midea also builds units for several other brands, and it holds the Toshiba home-appliance license in the U.S.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Toshiba dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Find the model number on the rating label on the back or side of the unit, then search it on Toshiba's home-appliance support site or the retailer's listing to download the PDF manual.

faqs.q: How do I clean a Toshiba dehumidifier filter?
faqs.a: Slide the mesh filter out from behind the intake grille, rinse it with lukewarm water, let it air-dry fully and slide it back in. Do this every couple of weeks in humid weather.

faqs.q: Has a Toshiba dehumidifier ever been recalled?
faqs.a: We found no CPSC dehumidifier recall under the Toshiba name. Because Midea builds them, and Midea-made units sold under other brands were recalled in 2016, check the manufacture date on any older secondhand unit.

faqs.q: Does the Toshiba 50-pint dehumidifier have a pump?
faqs.a: The standard TDDP5013ES2 does not; it uses a gravity hose or its internal tank. The TDDP5014RES2 is the pump-equipped version for basements without a nearby floor drain.
